_comment: Named baselines: a POINTER into evals/results/, never a copy of it. A second copy of a
number that can drift is the failure mode phase 3 hit three times in one day, so the stored
run stays the only place the figures live and this file only gives them names.
Every commit below was read out of the file it names, not remembered. The first draft of the
spec pointed python-2.8 at a run from 2026-09-11, which is c536cab — that is step 2.6.
pairedWith names the other run of the same state. The suite is run TWICE whenever HyDE is
involved, and one run is not a measurement of a flaky case; a diff against a single file is
a diff against one of a pair, and the reader should be able to find the other one.

ts-baseline.note: The TypeScript pipeline on main. The figure the README cites and every Python run is compared against. No target field: it predates there being a second one.

python-2.8.note: The Python port at parity, local. The 2.8 done-when run.

aws-2b.note: The same service deployed on ECS Express Mode, since torn down. Its pair ran with a dirty tree and says so in the file.

python-3.5b.note: The planner scope paragraph. The last state before the labelled GitHub set existed, so a diff forward from here cannot compare the GitHub metrics and will say so.

python-3.6.note: First contact with the labelled set: every process metric at ceiling, answer accuracy 24 of 52 across the pair.

python-3.6b.note: The identifier rule and EXCESSIVE_PAGINATION. 29 of 52 across the pair, and the run where gh-issue-1-author fell over the lookup budget.

python-3.6c.note: The lookup cap bounding looking rather than the turn. 31 of 52 across the pair, validity 43 of 43. The state phase 5 starts from, and what the restructure must diff empty against.
